record.context_brief: upgrading non-negative to positive sectional curvature
record.original_question: If a manifold has finite fundamental group and admits a metric of non-negative sectional curvature, must it also admit a metric of positive sectional curvature?

evidence.quote: Question 4.1. If a manifold has finite fundamental group and has non-negative sectional curvature, does it admit a metric of positive sectional curvature ?

artifact.self_contained_problem: Let $M$ be a smooth closed (compact, without boundary) connected manifold whose fundamental group $\pi_1(M)$ is finite, and suppose that $M$ admits a Riemannian metric $g_0$ of non-negative sectional curvature (i.e., $\sec_{g_0}(\sigma) \geq 0$ for every tangent 2-plane $\sigma$). Must $M$ then admit a Riemannian metric $g_1$ of strictly positive sectional curvature (i.e., $\sec_{g_1}(\sigma) > 0$ for every tangent 2-plane $\sigma$)?
artifact.status_search_result: The question is widely regarded as a major open problem in Riemannian geometry. The well-known case of $S^2\times S^2$ (the Hopf conjecture) is a special instance and remains unresolved; surveys (e.g., Wilking's survey and the AIM problem list compiled by M. Kerin) describe distinguishing the classes of non-negatively and positively curved manifolds as extremely hard and open.

status_evidence.title: Hopf conjecture - Wikipedia
status_evidence.snippet: Whether S^2 x S^2 admits a Riemannian metric with positive sectional curvature is a famous open problem.
status_evidence.claim: A canonical special case (S^2 x S^2) of the question is open.

status_evidence.title: Nonnegatively and Positively curved Manifolds (Wilking)
status_evidence.snippet: Distinguishing the classes K>=0 and K>0 is an extremely hard problem.
status_evidence.claim: The general gap between nonnegative and positive sectional curvature is open.

status_evidence.title: Open Problems in Non-negative Sectional Curvature (Kerin)
status_evidence.snippet: Compiled list of open problems concerning nonnegative sectional curvature.
status_evidence.claim: The problem appears in current open-problem compilations.
